name: illustrator-scoreboard-lower-third
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 28.6 - Export As > SVG, Styling: Internal CSS, Images: Embed, Responsive on
story: A student drew the match score as a lower third: two slanted club plates drawn with the pen tool, a score block between them with the period on an amber tab underneath, each club's crest embedded beside its name, and a red goal flash over each plate switched off in the layers panel. They named the layers the way docs/SVG_AUTHORING.md section 5b suggests - Team 1, Score 1, Flash 1 - and typed the period in Finnish, so Illustrator split it at the Ä.
idioms: Generator comment naming the SVG Export Plug-In build
Responsive export: viewBox only, no width/height attributes
<style type="text/css"> holding one property per .stN class, and one class carrying two properties
slanted plates as <polygon points="..."> with the trailing tab Illustrator leaves inside the attribute
two hidden flash layers exported as class="st10" whose rule is display:none
two pictures embedded as <image style="overflow:visible;"> positioned by transform alone
an accented word written as two <tspan> runs split at the non-ASCII character, with the class on the RUNS and nothing on the <text>
_x20_ escapes with data-name on every named layer
whyThisMatters: The scoreboard every student sports show draws: not a rectangle anywhere under the club names. Illustrator writes a slanted plate as a <polygon>, and until 2026-09-21 the mapping step knew only rectangles and rectangle-shaped paths, so both club names read 'On the artwork - no box of their own, so nothing grows around them' on a plate they plainly sit on, while the runtime was measuring their room against that very polygon. The period carries the run-styled <tspan> shape the Save As quiz does, arriving through an accented character. e2e/import-svg-behaviour.spec.ts walks this file to air.
